query: What operational burdens appear in incident descriptions?

per_column.name: primary_impacted_system
per_column.rationale: The affected system/asset is a constitutive aspect of what the operational burden is about -- it characterizes WHERE the burden falls, an intrinsic dimension of the burden itself rather than an external predictor.

per_column.name: issue_severity_indicator
per_column.rationale: The nature/severity of the failure (access failure, service unavailable/degraded, config error) is an aspect OF the burden -- it describes what kind of disruption constitutes the burden.

per_column.name: scope_of_impact
per_column.rationale: Breadth of impact (individual vs enterprise-wide) is a genuine constitutive dimension of operational burden: how much of the organization the burden weighs on.

per_column.name: resolution_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: The effort/complexity required to resolve is arguably the operational cost dimension of the burden -- an aspect of how burdensome it is to handle, thus a facet of the burden rather than an external cause.

judge.rationale: All four columns are genuine meronymic facets of operational burden: WHERE it lands (impacted system), WHAT kind of disruption (severity/failure type), HOW BROAD (scope), and HOW COSTLY to resolve (resolution complexity). These carve mostly distinct aspects. Mutual exclusivity is somewhat reduced because issue_severity_indicator and resolution_complexity_signal partially co-vary/overlap: 'service_unavailable/access_failure' severity strongly correlates with and is partly restated by 'routine_access_restore/infrastructure_intervention' resolution categories, so the failure-nature and resolution-effort facets blur together. Exhaustiveness is good but not complete: burden dimensions such as temporal duration/persistence (how long the burden lasts) and volume/frequency (recurrence) of the burden are not captured. Overall a coherent, largely MECE faceted decomposition with minor overlap and a couple of missing constitutive aspects.
